So it seems that whenever podman runs in order to log in,  it actually opens a bunch of websites while the container installs.  We obviously don't want that.

What the spec step said it changed, its final output:

The websites most likely opened because of the old rule that "any login URL the command prints opens in the browser". The login view also shows the image build's output, and package installs print plenty of URLs, so each one was being opened. I changed the spec so only the harness's own sign-in link ever opens, and only once. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 81 files.

## What changed in the spec

New text in `spec/scope/container-environment/index.pi`, under `#logging-in` (`.claude/reference/scope/container-environment/index.md#logging-in`):

- **Login output only:** URLs are watched for only once the login command has started. Anything the image build or Podman prints while pulling, building or starting the container is shown as text and never opened; at most its URLs are clickable.
- **Sign-in URLs only:** a URL opens only if it leads to the harness's sign-in, for example:
  - Claude Code's link to claude.ai or console.anthropic.com
  - Codex's link to auth.openai.com
  - OpenCode's link to whichever provider it's logging in with
  - a localhost callback the login asks to be visited

  Links to documentation, release notes or package homepages are only shown.
- **One URL at most:** a login opens at most one URL by itself, the first sign-in one. Any later sign-in URL is shown as a link for you to click.
- **Nothing recognized, nothing opened:** if no sign-in URL is recognized, nothing opens and every URL the command printed is shown as a link.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791218318-PreventPodmanFromOpeningWebsites.understanding.md`.

## Anchors the code should follow
- `ContainerEnvironmentScope`: `#logging-in`, for which output is watched for URLs, which URLs count as sign-in, and the open-once rule. Also `#image`, since build output goes to the login view and must not be scanned for URLs to open.
- `WelcomeScope` and `SettingsWindowScope`: both start the same login view, so the fix covers them too.

Any other URL it prints, as a link to documentation, release notes, or a package's homepage, is only shown. A login opens at most one URL by itself, the first such one; any later is shown as a link, for the user to click. Where no URL is recognized, nothing opens, and the view shows every URL the command printed as a link instead.

content.text:
The login view no longer opens the URLs the image build prints. Only the harness's own sign-in link opens, at most once. All 530 tests pass, including a new one for which URLs count as sign-ins. I haven't run a real login against Podman.

**What was happening:** the login view opened any URL that appeared in its output. That output includes the image build, where package installs print lots of links (npm, Debian, GitHub), so each one opened in your browser.

**What changed** (`src/login_view.rs`, plus `is_sign_in` in `src/container.rs`):
- **Only the login's own output is checked.** Nothing is opened from what the image build or Podman prints before the login command starts.
- **Only sign-in links open:**
  - Claude Code: claude.ai or console.anthropic.com.
  - Codex: auth.openai.com.
  - OpenCode: one of those, GitHub's device login, or opencode.ai's sign-in.
  - Any harness: a localhost callback.
- **At most one opens per login,** the first sign-in link. If nothing matches, nothing opens.
- **Every URL in the view is clickable,** build output included, so you can open any of them yourself. That covers later sign-in links and the case where none is recognized.
- **No half-printed links:** only finished lines are checked, so a URL still being printed is never opened cut short.

**Choices of mine:**
- **OpenCode's sign-in sites:** the spec says "the provider it is logging in with" without naming them, so I chose the list above.
- **Look-alike sites:** a site that only resembles claude.ai, such as `claude.ai.evil.example`, doesn't count.

The spec and the prompt agree.
